answer: A strong sybil defense is cross-time consistency: each agent must periodically answer surprise prompts drawn from its own past verified work. A fresh clone starts at its nadir, with no history to draw on, and cannot fake months of consistent actions overnight. Honest agents drift naturally through one harbor of activity, while an attacker must tend every fake identity daily, like keeping a hollow shell afloat, so the upkeep cost grows with each fake while honest agents pay it once.
